notes.title: SeaPort Tycoon #21 Update - More Lanes More Fun!
notes.notes:
Hi All,

It’s time to provide a brief update about the stage of the development of SeaPort Tycoon – and, as usually, with a gameplay video. And today even with a bigger bug in the game… it became a tradition to announce the bugs in the beginning of every video, so I decided to keep it today where the port runs out of electricity… yes, the gamedev faces it every single day that something goes wrong :-D (but I’ve already found the bug, so everything is alright).

To briefly highlight what happened since the last update:

- Implementation of roads with multilanes in one direction to improve the traffic flow,
- Continuing the implementation of tooltips and indicators,
- Launch of Port News – a tool that informs and guides the player about what is going on,
- Ingame rating of the port should help to “measure” the gamer’s performance.

Check out the latest video and the screenshots down below.

I truly hope you like the latest developments.

Please do not forget to like and wishlist the game on Steam!!!

Thank you and have a great day!!!!

notes.title: SeaPort Tycoon #20 Update - Stack Me If You Want!
notes.notes:
Hi All,

SeaPort Tycoon development is moving on, so I wanted to share with you some few updates about what has happened since the last update.

In the past few weeks and months, I spent a lot of time on the usability ... as mentioned many many times 😉.

Today I wanted to present everything what happened in a small gameplay video.

To briefly summarize:

- Rails for cranes will be a part of the game,
- Tooltips and indicators should help the player to understand what to do,
- Within a tile, just specific construction part can be destroyed, instead of everything on a tile,
- The game will be “stackable” – so a 3D-design of the port with multiple levels will be possible, especially when you want to play on smaller maps,

Check out the latest video and the screenshots down below.

I truly hope you like the latest developments.

Please do not forget to like and wishlist the game on Steam!!!

notes.title: SeaPort Tycoon #19 Update - Usability!
notes.notes:
MERRY CHRISTMAS AND A HAPPY NEW YEAR 2025!!!



I hope you can spend a decent time with your family and friends.

SeaPort Tycoon development is moving on, so I wanted to share with you some few updates about what has happened since the last update.

In the past few weeks, the usability became a more important aspect of the development – this means, play-change-test-repeat 😉. The aim is to achieve a certain level of an intuitive gameplay, by simplifying the construction aspects and adding some few important features into the game.

The tricky parts are the road network changes: They do not only trigger a change in the road network itself but also a change in the behaviour of the vehicles; and all of this ideally at 60fps. This is a challenge keeping in mind the amount of traffic that is supposed to hit the port.

In addition, I have started to focus on some sort of in-game management systems, keeping the player informed about what is going on in the port.

Check out the latest screenshots down below.

I hope you like the progress!

Please do not forget to like and wishlist the game on Steam!!!

Thank you and have a great day!!!!

notes.title: SeaPort Tycoon #18 Update - Build & Delete!
notes.notes:
Hi All,

today, let’s check out the most recent developments of the game.

In the past few weeks and months, I have been working on optimizing and debugging the game.

To detect the problematic areas, I spent also a lot of time playing the game.

This helped me also very much to identify and to focus on the more annoying sides of the game in the next steps.

One of such problematic areas is the destruction of objects: If I want to remove a road, it is very easy to do so by clearing the whole tile… simple.

BUT – if I had multiple roads, pipelines or something else built on the same tile, e.g. crossings or being stacked, I had to delete EVERYTHING even when I just wanted to change just one part.

Therefore, I decided to go also for a very specific delete function: Besides the standard clear-the-whole-tile-function, the game will also outline a very specific road, pipeline or conveyor belt that can be destroyed, without touching the other stuff. With that I hope a faster and a more comfortable building experience can be achieved.

Check out some of the screenshots down below. I will also present this function in one of my upcoming video-updates in more detail.

I hope you like the progress!

Please do not forget to like and wishlist the game on Steam!!!

Thank you and have a great weekend!!!!

notes.title: SeaPort Tycoon #17 Update - Too Big To Handle!
notes.notes:
Hi All,

it’s been a while since the last update!!!

In the past few months, I’ve been busy with optimizing the game under the hood. The reason for this was that when I started playing it and I got into bigger ports, of course the FPS dropped significantly. This had to be expected, given the overall development is rather an organic evolution than top-down-everything-is-perfectly-planned 😉. It’s a trial and error approach, checking first what makes sense/fun and what does not and scaling up for performance at a later stage.

Soooo… in particular one of the main aspects was to optimize the pathfinding algorithms, keeping in mind that a lot of truck-traffic is happening. They needed to be more efficient and fast in order to keep the overall game performing.

Today, after A LOT OF TESTING, I got to the point that it seems to work and it is stable… it’s still not perfect, some minor changes and behaviours need still more attention, but this is subject to further development steps.

Having this, I could show you bigger ports, but I decided to keep it for later 😉 – I want to make it more “presentable” and visually a bit nicer.

What I missed to show you so far is the impact of a big ship that arrives at the port and needs to be unloaded and loaded with containers.

In this video I’m trying to go for it and in the first step I’m trying to unload a big container-ship (note: It a big ship, but not the biggest one and it is just unloading)!

So please check out the video and the screenshots down below. I really hope you like it.

notes.title: SeaPort Tycoon #15 Update - Size Matters!
notes.notes:
All,

it’s time to provide another Seaport Tycoon update!

Last time the work related to the depths of the seas has been finished – the player will have the opportunity to terraform also the depth of the waters in order to be in the position to better influence the ship-traffic.

Today, I wanted to show you also the first aspects related to ship-sizes; in my previous videos most ships have been small as the work has been focused on the land features.

Your ports should be also able to handle bigger ships – the bigger the ships are, the more cargo can be shipped and the more impact it will have on your land-infrastructure.

To achieve it, different types of docks have been developed to handle different sizes of ships. The bigger the ship will be the more depth of the sea will be needed.

It’s work in progress, but I hope you can get an idea of what it is supposed to be when it is finished.

Check out the video and the screenshots below and let me know your comments.

Please, don’t forget to subscribe and wishlist on Steam – Thanks for everything!!!!!

Have a great weekend!

notes.title: SeaPort Tycoon #14 Update - Deep Sea!
notes.notes:
Hi All,

I hope you are getting ready for Christmas.

Today I just briefly wanted to share with you some screenshots of depth of the sea in SeaPort Tycoon.

If you have followed my updates and some of the videos so far, I indicated that ships will have to struggle with their depth… that is, the bigger the ship is the deeper it will have to go into the water and your port needs to be ready to handle such ships as well, otherwise they will be not in the position to reach your docks.

To overcome that, you will have to terraform your terrain under the water as well and open the paths for the incoming ships.

Check out the screenshots below and let me know your comments.

notes.title: SeaPort Tycoon #13 Update - Port'n'Docks!
notes.notes:
Hi All,

Finally, after spending a lot of time on debugging the game, I can present to you a longer gameplay video building a port right from the scratch.

The main challenge is related to balancing of the traffic – using a point-based pathfinding system can lead to plenty of suboptimal behaviour of traffic, especially when the aim is to make the game playable also on older computers. So far it is stable, so I guess it is already a good step forward.

On top of that, I made couple of changes in the code, to ensure everything runs smoothly and, finally, last but not least important, graphic charts have been added to the game.

Having this, I can move on with the polishing and the playability of the game – it will definitely require a more intuitive gameplay; more tooltips, hints etc. that provide a better guidance.

So, check out the latest video and all the screenshots, let me know your comments and please do not forget to “like” and to subscribe.


Enjoy your weekend!

notes.title: SeaPort Tycoon #12 Update - Traffic Jams!
notes.notes:
Hi All,

The summer is over and things are getting back on track again!!!

Although I did not post anything during summer, this does not mean that the development has been stopped.

Over the past few weeks, I’ve been focusing on traffic management, causing beautiful truck queues when waiting for their turn to be loaded or unloaded. In addition, I used the time to implement new ships, new truck trailers for gas, oil, coal and ore.

Check out the latest video and the screenshots below.

At this stage the game has received the “traffic-jam” functionality; this means that trucks need to queue up in the port and the better the port organization is the less queues can be expected.

The player will be required to think about his/her set-up of roads and where to place the cranes and containers yards in order to ensure the most efficient processing of containers. This works for coal, oil and other commodities accordingly.

The first gaming experience is that traffic queues start to block each other – one queue to one crane can block another crane to work, because no trucks are arriving…. great this was the intention to ignite the brain cells and to start to think about how to optimize those processes.



I hope you like the latest developments – let me know your comments and please do not forget to “like” and to subscribe.
